examples.solution_text:
Test integer factors of the constant term.
$\begin{align*}P(-2)&=-16+28-8-4\\&=0\end{align*}$
Test the derivatives at this zero.
$\begin{align*}P'(x)&=6x^{2}+14x+4\\P'(-2)&=24-28+4\\&=0\\P''(x)&=12x+14\\P''(-2)&=-10\end{align*}$
So $-2$ has multiplicity exactly $2$.
Let the remaining zero be $\alpha$. Counting the repeated zero twice, use the sum of the zeroes.
$\begin{align*}-2-2+\alpha&=-\frac{7}{2}\\\alpha&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$
Include the leading coefficient when writing the factors.
$\begin{align*}P(x)&=2(x+2)^{2}\left(x-\frac{1}{2}\right)\\&=(x+2)^{2}(2x-1)\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Factorise $P(x)=8x^{4}-12x^{3}-30x^{2}-17x-3$ using calculus. Hint: try fractions.
examples.solution_text:
The leading coefficient is $8$, so rational candidates include fractions with denominators dividing $8$.
$\begin{align*}P\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)&=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{2}-\frac{15}{2}+\frac{17}{2}-3\\&=0\end{align*}$
Test successive derivatives.
$\begin{align*}P'(x)&=32x^{3}-36x^{2}-60x-17\\P'\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)&=-4-9+30-17\\&=0\\P''(x)&=96x^{2}-72x-60\\P''\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)&=24+36-60\\&=0\\P'''(x)&=192x-72\\P'''\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)&=-168\end{align*}$
So $-\frac{1}{2}$ has multiplicity exactly $3$.
Let the remaining zero be $\alpha$. A quartic's zeroes have product equal to the constant term divided by the leading coefficient.
$\begin{align*}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3}\alpha&=-\frac{3}{8}\\-\frac{\alpha}{8}&=-\frac{3}{8}\\\alpha&=3\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}P(x)&=8\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3}(x-3)\\&=(2x+1)^{3}(x-3)\end{align*}$

Test a factor of the constant term.
$\begin{align*}P(3)&=27-81+81-27\\&=0\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}P'(x)&=3x^{2}-18x+27\\P'(3)&=27-54+27\\&=0\\P''(x)&=6x-18\\P''(3)&=0\end{align*}$
The zero at $3$ has multiplicity at least $3$. This is the whole degree, so its multiplicity is exactly $3$ and there are no remaining zeroes.
$P(x)=(x-3)^{3}$

examples.question_text: Solve $x^{4}-6x^{3}+10x^{2}-6x+1=0$, given that it has a repeated root.
examples.solution_text:
Let $P(x)=x^{4}-6x^{3}+10x^{2}-6x+1$. Test a factor of the constant term.
$\begin{align*}P(1)&=1-6+10-6+1\\&=0\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}P'(x)&=4x^{3}-18x^{2}+20x-6\\P'(1)&=4-18+20-6\\&=0\\P''(x)&=12x^{2}-36x+20\\P''(1)&=-4\end{align*}$
So $1$ has multiplicity exactly $2$.
Let the remaining roots be $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Use their sum and product.
$\begin{align*}1+1+\alpha+\beta&=6\\\alpha+\beta&=4\\(1)(1)\alpha\beta&=1\\\alpha\beta&=1\end{align*}$
The remaining roots satisfy $t^{2}-4t+1=0$.
$\begin{align*}t&=\frac{4\pm\sqrt{16-4}}{2}\\&=2\pm\sqrt{3}\end{align*}$
The solutions are $x=1$ (twice), $x=2+\sqrt{3}$ and $x=2-\sqrt{3}$.

examples.question_text: The polynomial $P(x)=4x^{4}-20x^{3}+13x^{2}+30x+9$ has two repeated zeroes. Factorise it completely using calculus.
examples.solution_text:
Test rational candidates, including fractions whose denominators divide $4$.
$\begin{align*}P(3)&=324-540+117+90+9\\&=0\\P\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)&=\frac{1}{4}+\frac{5}{2}+\frac{13}{4}-15+9\\&=0\end{align*}$
$P'(x)=16x^{3}-60x^{2}+26x+30$.
$\begin{align*}P'(3)&=432-540+78+30\\&=0\\P'\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)&=-2-15-13+30\\&=0\end{align*}$
Both zeroes have multiplicity at least $2$. Their lower bounds total the degree $4$, so both have multiplicity exactly $2$.
$\begin{align*}P(x)&=4\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}(x-3)^{2}\\&=(2x+1)^{2}(x-3)^{2}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Find the quartic polynomial with a triple zero at $x=2$, a simple zero at $x=-3$ and $P(0)=12$. Give your answer in factored form.
examples.solution_text:
The multiplicities give the factors; use the given value to find the scale factor.
$P(x)=k(x-2)^{3}(x+3)$.
$\begin{align*}P(0)&=k(-2)^{3}(3)\\12&=-24k\\k&=-\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$
$P(x)=-\frac{1}{2}(x-2)^{3}(x+3)$.

examples.derivation: P(-2)=0; P'(x)=6x²+14x+4 gives P'(-2)=0; P''(-2)=-10, establishing multiplicity 2. The root sum is -7/2, so the remaining root is 1/2. Expanding (x+2)²(2x-1) gives 2x³+7x²+4x-4.

At -1/2, P=1/2+3/2-15/2+17/2-3=0, P'=-4-9+30-17=0 and P''=24+36-60=0. P'''(-1/2)=-168 establishes multiplicity 3. The quartic root product gives (-1/8)α=-3/8, hence α=3. Expanding (2x+1)³(x-3) reproduces the stated polynomial.
P(3)=27-81+81-27=0; P'(3)=27-54+27=0; P''(3)=18-18=0. Multiplicity is at least 3 and exhausts the cubic degree. Expanding (x-3)³ reproduces P(x).
P(1)=0, P'(1)=0 and P''(1)=12-36+20=-4, so 1 is exactly a double root. The remaining roots have sum 4 and product 1, giving t²-4t+1=0 and t=2±√3. Expanding (x-1)²(x²-4x+1) reproduces the equation.

P(3)=324-540+117+90+9=0 and P(-1/2)=1/4+5/2+13/4-15+9=0. P'(3)=432-540+78+30=0 and P'(-1/2)=-2-15-13+30=0. Two distinct roots each have multiplicity at least 2, exhausting degree 4. Expanding (2x+1)²(x-3)² gives the stated polynomial with leading coefficient 4.
The prescribed multiplicities give P(x)=k(x-2)³(x+3). Substitution at zero gives 12=-24k, hence k=-1/2. The resulting quartic has exactly the prescribed triple and simple zeroes and P(0)=12.
